incidents.root_cause: TB-BH wireless backhaul link to the core site degraded (signal -81 to -87 dBm warnings) and then dropped; TB-AP1 and TB-BH were silent until the link returned
RF interference on TA-AP1 wlan1 at 5745 MHz (source not identified in the logs); cleared by an admin channel change to 5805 MHz
Repeated SSH login attempts against CORE-RTR from 203.0.113.45; all 10 attempts failed

test_questions.q: What warnings appeared on TB-BH before the Tower B outage, and when?
test_questions.a: Three bh-signal-check script warnings: 02:01:04 (-81 dBm), 02:04:37 (-84 dBm), 02:07:19 (-87 dBm).

test_questions.q: When did TB-BH and TB-AP1 stop sending logs, and when did they resume?
test_questions.a: The last line from Tower B devices was TB-BH at 02:10:02 (disconnected, extensive data loss). Nothing came from TB-BH or TB-AP1 until TB-BH connected at 04:35:09.

test_questions.q: When did the first Tower B PPPoE session drop in the overnight outage, and when did the last one reconnect?
test_questions.a: The first drop (terminating, peer not responding) was at 02:10:07. The last session reconnected at 04:39:26. All 15 Tower B customers were affected.

test_questions.q: Which source IP attacked CORE-RTR over SSH, how many login failures were logged, and when?
test_questions.a: 203.0.113.45. There were 10 failures from 11:38:16 to 11:47:54 (users: admin x7, root x2, user x1), each preceded by a firewall SYN line to port 22.

test_questions.q: Which Tower A customers lost their PPPoE session during the afternoon interference, and what ended it?
test_questions.a: cust-A002, A005, A008, A011 and A013 (11 PPPoE disconnects between 14:23:09 and 15:02:24). An admin logged in to TA-AP1 at 15:01:14 and changed the wlan1 frequency from 5745 to 5805 at 15:02:31.

test_questions.q: When did CORE-RTR log high-CPU warnings?
What external device or source caused the interference on TA-AP1?
What RouterOS firmware version is running on TB-BH?
